cleanIntro: Morini's interval for this pistol is blunt: strip and clean every 500 rounds. The strip itself is one torx screw at the front of the trigger guard and the top slide lifts off — and then a small movement most people get wrong the first time, easing the action rearward, pushing it down and sliding it forward again. ⛔ The trigger unit gets cleaned and DRIED, never oiled; one drop on the sear is the entire permitted lubrication in that area.

steps.title: Slide open and latched, then the magazine out
steps.action: Open the slide and latch it back on the slide stop before you touch the magazine — that order leaves the chamber visible while your other hand is busy. Then push the magazine catch forward with your thumb and take the magazine out.
steps.aside: Push the magazine catch forward with your thumb and remove the magazine.
steps.quote: Open the slide and latch it with the slide stop.
steps.cite: Morini CM 22M RF Sport Pistol Instruction Manual — Manual CM22M RF EN-DE-IT-FR (file title on morini.ch's downloads index) — 1. LOADING AND FIRING, printed p.5

steps.title: Release the hammer spring before it goes in the case
steps.action: Morini asks for the hammer spring to be relaxed when shooting is finished, and it can only be done with the slide CLOSED and the magazine OUT: pull the slide back slightly, let it run forward, then press the trigger. Do this pointing somewhere safe, and only after you have seen the chamber empty.
steps.caution: The magazine must be removed from the pistol.
steps.quote: A slight pull rearward on the closed slide will set the mechanism after which the trigger can be pulled relieving the hammer spring.
steps.cite: Morini CM 22M RF Sport Pistol Instruction Manual — Manual CM22M RF EN-DE-IT-FR (file title on morini.ch's downloads index) — 2. UNLOADING, printed p.5

steps.title: One torx screw at the front of the trigger guard
steps.action: Loosen the torx screw at the front of the trigger guard and lift the top slide off the main frame. It is the only fastener between the two halves of the pistol.
steps.quote: Loosen the torx screw at the front of the trigger guard and dismount the top slide from
steps.cite: Morini CM 22M RF Sport Pistol Instruction Manual — Manual CM22M RF EN-DE-IT-FR (file title on morini.ch's downloads index) — 6. DISASSEMBLY, printed p.7

steps.title: Rearward, down, forward — the movement that frees the action
steps.action: Ease the action rearward, then push it down and slide it forward again. That three-part motion is what clears the action out of its rails; forcing it straight back or straight up will not work and will mark the rails. If it does not want to go, you have not eased it far enough back before pushing down.
steps.quote: Ease the action rearward then push down and slide forward again.
steps.cite: Morini CM 22M RF Sport Pistol Instruction Manual — Manual CM22M RF EN-DE-IT-FR (file title on morini.ch's downloads index) — 6. DISASSEMBLY, printed p.7

steps.title: Grip off, and that is the published strip
steps.action: Undo the grip retaining allen screw and remove both. That completes the four-step disassembly Morini publishes — there is no further breakdown of the action, the trigger unit or the frame in this book.
steps.quote: Undo the grip retaining allen screw and remove both.
steps.cite: Morini CM 22M RF Sport Pistol Instruction Manual — Manual CM22M RF EN-DE-IT-FR (file title on morini.ch's downloads index) — 6. DISASSEMBLY, printed p.7

steps.title: Phosphor bronze from the BREECH end, always
steps.action: Clean the barrel with a phosphor bronze or brass brush, and always work from the breech end — not from the muzzle. A rod entering at the muzzle wears the crown, and on a 25-metre pistol the crown is the accuracy. Then a nylon brush, a clean patch or .22 felts to take the excess cleaner out.
steps.quote: Use a phosphor bronze or brass brush initially to clean the barrel. This should always be carried out from the breech end.
steps.cite: Morini CM 22M RF Sport Pistol Instruction Manual — Manual CM22M RF EN-DE-IT-FR (file title on morini.ch's downloads index) — 10. CLEANING, printed p.7

steps.title: Trigger assembly: clean, dry, and ONE drop on the sear
steps.action: Clean the trigger assembly and dry it. ⛔ No aerosol, no oil in the unit — the one permitted exception is a single drop on the sear. Everything else on the pistol gets a cloth, a light brush or compressed air.
steps.caution: Never use aerosol lubricants or oils within the trigger unit however one drop of oil may be applied to the sear only.
steps.quote: Clean and dry the trigger assembly.
steps.cite: Morini CM 22M RF Sport Pistol Instruction Manual — Manual CM22M RF EN-DE-IT-FR (file title on morini.ch's downloads index) — 10. CLEANING, printed p.7

steps.title: Silicone cloth outside — and never a damp rug
steps.action: Wipe the outside down with a silicone cloth or one carrying the lightest film of oil before it goes away. Morini names the failure directly: a pistol left to sweat in a damp rug, or stored where the temperature swings, rusts and the materials deteriorate. That is a stored-gun problem, not a shooting one.
steps.quote: Never leave your weapon to sweat or perspire within a damp pistol rug or in storage exposed to extreme changes of temperature or atmosphere, as this will cause rusting and deterioration of the materials.
steps.cite: Morini CM 22M RF Sport Pistol Instruction Manual — Manual CM22M RF EN-DE-IT-FR (file title on morini.ch's downloads index) — 10. CLEANING, printed p.7

deepAbsentReason: Morini publishes NO strip deeper than the four steps in the guided clean above — top slide off, action out, grip off, and stop. The book carries hammer-spring tension and recoil-buffer adjustments after that, but they are ADJUSTMENTS made with the pistol assembled, not a teardown. There is no published route into the trigger unit, and the reason is printed in the cleaning section: the trigger assembly is to be cleaned and dried, never oiled, with a single drop on the sear as the only exception. ⚠ Morini also states that using force while stripping the gun, or the use of non-original spare parts, discharges the manufacturer from any warranty, and recommends the pistol be tested by an authorised gunsmith from time to time. Nothing deeper is presented here and none has been invented.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Phosphor bronze or brass brush — from the BREECH end, always
Nylon brush, clean patch or .22 felts to lift excess cleaner

cleaning.name: ACTION & FRAME
tasks: Cloth, light brush or compressed air
Rails wiped where the action rides

cleaning.name: ⛔ TRIGGER UNIT
tasks: No aerosol, no oil in the unit
ONE drop on the sear — that is the whole permitted lubrication

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Silicone cloth or the lightest oil film before storage
⚠ Never left in a damp rug or in swinging temperatures

reassembly: Reverse of the strip: grip on, action into its rails, top slide onto the frame.
⛔ Grip retaining screw AND the frame attachment screw both securely tightened — the book names both.
Slide worked by hand and allowed to close under its own spring, never ridden.
Chamber checked clear before the magazine goes anywhere near it.
fncheck: Back together and empty: check the grip retaining screw and the frame attachment screw are both securely tightened — Morini names both by name in the reassembly note. Work the slide by hand and let it run forward under its own spring; do not ride it. Latch it open on the slide stop and look through the chamber.
